chunks: And from him, from Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from some of our companions, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

I asked him about a man who marries a female slave belonging to a group of people [or: a man marries a slave woman], [regarding] whether the children are slaves or free. He said, 'If one of the parents is free, then the children are free.'
ai.seo_question: What is the status of children born to a free man and a slave woman in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies the principle of *'itq* (manumission) in mixed-status unions, establishing that the offspring of a free person and a slave woman are free (*ahrar*), a ruling derived from the status of the free parent. This principle is foundational in Shia jurisprudence for determining the inheritance of social and legal status, ensuring that the child is not bound by the lower status of the slave parent. It reflects the broader Islamic emphasis on the gradual emancipation of slaves and the elevation of their descendants.
